This study introduces a novel adaptive message transmission-based particle filter (AMTPDA) algorithm designed for robust radio-based localization and tracking. The proposed method employs a hybrid approach, integrating the advantages of both the adaptive multiple hypothesis PDA (AMHPDA) and the adaptive multiple model PDA (AMPDA). Specifically, it utilizes the AMHPDA framework to determine the optimal number of target tracks and the AMPPDA framework to dynamically adjust the measurement noise covariance matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that the AMTPDA algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of robustness and accuracy.

This study presents the first measurement of the joint-polarization states in $W^{\pm}Z$ production, utilizing $pp$ collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The analysis covers an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb$^{-1}$, yielding 110,000 $W^{\pm}Z$ events after selection. The observed polarization fractions for the $W$ and $Z$ bosons align with Standard Model predictions, and the results are reported as ratios relative to these theoretical expectations.

We introduce a novel framework for characterizing gravitational fields, termed the "fabric tensor." This approach offers a fresh perspective on the Einstein field equations, which are reinterpreted as a set of conservation laws for the fabric tensor. By examining the properties of this tensor, we demonstrate that it is traceless and possesses a specific algebraic structure, thereby establishing its classification as a type D Weyl tensor.

This paper introduces a topological dualism for orthomodular lattices, establishing a categorical equivalence between the category of orthomodular lattices and the category of topological spaces equipped with a specific type of closure operator.

This paper introduces coq-psv, a tool designed to render Coq proof scripts as interactive visualizations. The system supports various output formats, including HTML, PDF, and LaTeX, and is available at https://github.com/CoqPSV.
We establish a sharp upper bound for the fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms, a result that extends the findings of Blomer and Young to the case of arbitrary level and weight.

This study introduces a novel stopping criterion for Krylov subspace solvers, specifically designed for symmetric positive definite matrices. The approach relies on the observation that the residual norm of a Krylov solver is equivalent to the norm of a polynomial applied to a specific matrix, which is then minimized using a convex optimization technique. The authors demonstrate that this criterion is more effective than the standard one, particularly when dealing with ill-conditioned matrices. Furthermore, the paper presents a new variant of the barrier function used in Interior Point Methods (IPMs), which is solved using the proposed stopping rule. The authors also provide a theoretical analysis of the computational cost associated with this new IPM variant.

We present the calculation of the polarized variable-flavor number scheme (VFNS) transition matrix element $A_{gq}(N)$ at $O(\alpha_s^3)$, which is essential for determining the polarized gluon distribution within the framework of global QCD analyses.

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has led to widespread adoption across numerous sectors, yet this progress has also resulted in a surge of AI-related incidents. These events range from minor issues to catastrophic failures, causing significant harm to individuals and society. While the AI community has begun acknowledging the necessity of addressing these incidents, there remains a lack of a centralized repository for such data. This paper introduces the AI Incident Database (AID), a comprehensive catalog of AI-related events. AID offers a standardized format for incident reporting, enabling researchers to analyze the frequency and nature of these occurrences. Furthermore, it provides a framework for categorizing incidents and outlines strategies for mitigating their impact.

We introduce a novel exact renormalization group framework that employs gradient descent to minimize the distance between the renormalized action and a predefined reference action. This approach is demonstrated on the $\phi^4$ theory, where it is shown to yield results consistent with those from the Wilson-Polchik exact renormalization group.

This study introduces a novel framework for monitoring hybrid process descriptions that incorporate conflict management. We define a hybrid process description as a combination of a hybrid process model and a hybrid event log, where the former represents a workflow with continuous variables and the latter documents actual execution traces. The proposed framework utilizes a conflict manager to resolve discrepancies between these models and logs. We present an automata-theoretic approach to monitor these descriptions, which involves constructing a conflict manager by computing the synchronous product of a process model and a log-based automaton, followed by the removal of all paths that do not align with the process model. We demonstrate that this method is both sound and complete. Furthermore, we establish that the computational complexity of this approach is equivalent to that of the underlying process model.

This paper introduces a processor-based operational semantics for Proto-Quipper-M, a language designed for creating and simulating quantum circuits. We demonstrate that this processor model is equivalent to the established small-step semantics for Proto-Quipper-M. Furthermore, we establish the soundness of this processor semantics with respect to Proto-Quipper-M's type system.

We investigate the statistical properties of the largest eigenvalues within a broad class of random matrix models, demonstrating that their distributions exhibit universal scaling behavior. This finding is supported by both analytical derivations and numerical simulations, which reveal that the scaling exponents are determined by the model's parameters. Furthermore, we identify a critical point where the system undergoes a transition from a localized to a delocalized regime.

We investigate the creation of bosonic pairs and the emergence of squeezing within a system of long-lived dipoles interacting with a cavity. This setup is designed to facilitate the measurement of optical phases, and we demonstrate that the resulting nonclassical states can surpass the standard quantum limit.

Contig construction is a pivotal phase in de novo genome assembly, where the objective is to identify the optimal set of non-overlapping sequences that collectively encompass all read overlaps. This study introduces a distributed-memory parallel algorithm designed to address this challenge. The method employs a greedy strategy, iteratively selecting the read with the highest overlap count to form a new contig, and incorporates a novel technique for efficiently managing the read pool. Experimental results indicate that the algorithm achieves a speedup of 100x on a 1,000-node cluster, demonstrating its efficacy in assembling a 1.5 terabyte dataset of long-read sequences.

This study examines the delayed logistic equation with a new type of post-lag term, which is derived from a cell biological model. We establish the existence of a unique positive equilibrium and demonstrate that the system's dynamics are either globally stable or exhibit a unique positive periodic solution, contingent upon the delay parameter.

Statistical depth serves as a valuable tool for quantifying the centrality of a point within a dataset, with applications ranging from outlier detection to robust statistical estimation. This paper introduces a novel depth metric for point processes by adapting the isometric log-ratio (ILR) transformation to the space of probability measures. We demonstrate that this new depth function satisfies the fundamental axioms of statistical depth and provide a consistent estimator for it. Furthermore, we establish the consistency of a robust mean estimator derived from this depth metric.

This study introduces a hybrid machine that merges the benefits of superconducting hybrid machines with those of ideal superconducting machines. The analysis demonstrates that this new configuration can achieve a higher power density than the ideal superconducting hybrid machine.

The Gamow-Teller strength distribution for the $^{70-78}$Ge isotopes has been measured using the $(p,n)$ reaction at 25 MeV. The findings indicate that the Gamow-Teller strength is concentrated at low excitation energies, with a maximum occurring at approximately 10 MeV. This distribution aligns well with shell model predictions based on the $g_{9/2}$ and $d_{5/2}$ orbitals. Additionally, the study reveals a significant increase in the $g_{9/2}$ orbital occupation for $^{78}$Ge compared to $^{70}$Ge, a trend that supports the existence of a shell closure at $N$ = 40.

This study introduces a novel technique for determining the masses of short-lived nuclei by utilizing the magnetic field within a Penning trap. The method relies on measuring the cyclotron frequency of the ion, which is corrected for the trap's magnetic field inhomogeneity using the frequency of a co-trapped reference ion. The resulting mass precision is determined by the relative difference in their cyclotron frequencies. The authors demonstrate this method's validity through high-precision mass measurements of $^{10}$Be, $^{11}$Be, and $^{11}$B, achieving uncertainties of 1.5, 1.5, and 1.5 parts per billion, respectively.

We introduce a novel framework for discretizing continuous field theories, specifically designed to facilitate the application of modern machine learning techniques to lattice field theory. This approach is termed "standardizing flows," and it is demonstrated that this method can be utilized to generate configurations of the $O(N)$-symmetric $\phi^4$ model.

This study introduces a novel biasing technique for regular expression-based structured text recognition, designed to improve the accuracy of existing models. We demonstrate that this approach is compatible with current state-of-the-art systems and yields significant performance gains.

This study investigates top quark pair production in proton-nucleus collisions, utilizing the CDF II detector at the Tevatron. The analysis focuses on a final state characterized by two leptons, missing transverse energy, and at least four jets, with the requirement that at least one jet originates from a b-quark. The dataset comprises 10.3 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-antiproton collision data and 10.3 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-lead collision data, both collected at a center-of-mass energy of 980 GeV. The study establishes the first experimental upper limit on the top quark pair production cross section in proton-lead collisions, determined to be $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} < 1.1$ nb at a 95% confidence level. Additionally, the analysis presents the first measurement of the top quark pair production cross section in proton-antiproton collisions, yielding $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} = 7.0 \pm 1.4$ (stat) $\pm 1.0$ (syst) nb.

Cross-domain Text-to-SQL semantic interpretation involves converting natural language queries into SQL statements for specific database environments. Although existing methods have achieved significant success, they often struggle with generalization when facing new domains. To address this limitation, we introduce a new end-to-end framework that utilizes auxiliary tasks to enhance generalization capabilities. Specifically, we employ a domain-specific auxiliary task to guide the model in learning domain-invariant representations, thereby improving its ability to adapt to unseen domains. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

We present the results of a power spectrum analysis for the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) first data release, which covers 100 square degrees of the northern sky. The study examines 100 MHz radio sources with flux densities exceeding 1 mJy, utilizing a sample of 1,000,000 galaxies. We derive the galaxy bias parameter by comparing the observed power spectrum to the linear matter power spectrum, finding a value of $b=1.11 \pm 0.01$ for the brightest sources ($S>10$ mJy) and $b=1.15 \pm 0.01$ for the faintest sources ($S>1$ mJy). Additionally, we investigate the impact of source clustering on the bias estimate by analyzing the two-point correlation function of the brightest galaxies. We detect a significant excess in the correlation function at small angular separations, which we attribute to the clustering of radio sources within galaxies. This effect is modeled using a two-halo and one-halo framework, where the one-halo term is fitted with a double power law. We find that the excess is well described by a model assuming a mean galaxy mass of $\log(M_{\rm gal}/M_{\odot})=11.1$ and a halo mass of $\log(M_{\rm halo}/M_{\odot})=12.

The high-dimensional rank Lasso problem involves minimizing a convex combination of the $\ell_1$ norm and a rank loss function, which is a non-convex, discontinuous, and non-differentiable objective. This study introduces a highly efficient algorithm for solving this problem, leveraging a newly developed adaptive-sieving technique. The method's performance is validated through extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic data and real-world datasets.

We introduce a general framework for calculating entropy production in open quantum systems, applicable to arbitrary driving protocols. This approach is particularly effective for scenarios involving rapid and gentle driving, where it yields a convex expression for entropy generation. We demonstrate that this convex form is consistent with the established short-time limit of entropy production. Furthermore, we utilize this expression to derive a lower bound on the total entropy generation, which serves as a benchmark for evaluating the efficiency of specific driving protocols.

This study investigates the hidden environmental costs of AI-driven solutions for environmental challenges, specifically examining the carbon footprint of training and deploying these models. We analyze the energy consumption and associated emissions of various machine learning algorithms, including decision trees, random forests, and neural networks, across different datasets. Our findings reveal that while AI models can effectively address environmental issues, their development and implementation carry significant ecological burdens. We propose a framework for evaluating the environmental impact of AI systems and offer guidelines for developing more sustainable machine learning approaches.

Prescriptive procedure monitoring (PPM) is a specialized field within business process management (BPM) that focuses on the real-time analysis of process instances to generate actionable recommendations for improving execution. This paper offers a comprehensive review of the current state of PPM, examining its fundamental concepts, the various approaches to implementing it, and the associated challenges. Additionally, it outlines promising avenues for future research in this domain.

This study introduces a novel, multi-objective optimization framework for controlling heat in material processing, utilizing a generalized Boussinesq model. The approach employs a posteriori error estimation to guide the placement of heat sources, aiming to minimize both the deviation of the final state from a target and the total energy consumed. The resulting optimization problem is solved using a gradient-based algorithm, with the necessary gradients computed via an adjoint-state method. The effectiveness of this strategy is demonstrated through numerical experiments.

This paper introduces a kernelization approach for the stacking problem, enabling the use of kernel methods to identify optimal weights for the combined model. This study investigates how opinion dynamics evolve within social networks that are subject to preference-based flipping. We introduce a model where agents hold binary opinions and form ties with others who share their views, while simultaneously severing connections with those who hold opposing views. In this framework, an agent's stance can reverse if they are linked to a majority of individuals with a contrary opinion. We demonstrate that this system exhibits a dual dynamic: structural balance and opinion formation. We prove that the system converges to a state of structural balance, where the network partitions into two distinct groups, each internally cohesive and mutually disconnected. Furthermore, we show that opinions within these groups stabilize, with all members in a group adopting a uniform stance. We also provide a sufficient condition ensuring that both groups will hold different opinions. Finally, we analyze the impact of the preference-based flipping mechanism on the speed of convergence and the final distribution of opinions.

We investigate the internal structure of a specific class of black holes, termed "hairy dark stars," which are defined by a scalar field that remains non-zero at the event horizon. These objects are modeled as asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric configurations featuring a perfect fluid core. We demonstrate that the fluid's energy density and pressure diverge at the center, a result that aligns with the findings of recent studies on the external regions of these stars.

Transcriptional delays, defined as the time gap between the initiation of transcription and the release of a fully processed mRNA, are a critical yet poorly understood aspect of gene expression. This study introduces a genome-wide model of transcription dynamics that integrates experimental data on RNA polymerase (RNAP) movement and mRNA production rates. By fitting this model to data from *E. coli*, we identified a consistent delay of approximately 100 seconds for most genes, with a slight increase to 110 seconds for longer transcripts. Furthermore, we developed a method to estimate the delay for individual genes, revealing that this parameter varies significantly across the genome. We hypothesize that these variations reflect differences in the molecular mechanisms governing transcription, and we suggest that this heterogeneity may serve as a regulatory layer influencing gene expression.

The study of shape coexistence in 64Ni, a nucleus with 28 protons and 36 neutrons, is examined using the Interacting Boson Model (IBM). This analysis highlights the critical role of the monopole force in generating the observed low-lying 0+ states. The findings indicate that the interaction between neutron pairs in the d5/2 orbital and the monopole force is the primary driver of the energy gap between the ground state and the first excited 0+ state.

This paper investigates linear complementary pairs of group codes over finite primary ideal rings. We establish that a linear code over such a ring possesses a linear complementary dual if and only if its dual code is also self-orthogonal. Furthermore, we derive a formula for the size of linear codes with linear complementary duals over these rings.

This study introduces a compact representation for probability distributions over discrete variables, enabling more efficient exact inference in graphical models. We demonstrate that this approach accelerates the computation of the most probable explanation (MPE) and facilitates constrained optimization within these models.

We introduce a new asynchronous audio-visual framework designed to detect dropped objects, a task that is challenging due to the inherent difficulty in aligning audio and visual data. Our approach employs a two-stage strategy: first, we utilize a visual-only model to identify the object's location, and second, we refine this estimate by incorporating audio information. To achieve this, we develop a novel audio-visual attention mechanism that dynamically weights audio and visual inputs based on the specific task requirements. Additionally, we present a new dataset featuring synchronized audio and visual recordings of items falling from various heights. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We introduce a novel, data-driven methodology for analyzing shear thickening transitions in suspensions, which relies on the global scaling of the stress versus shear rate curve. This approach is capable of identifying the critical shear rate and the critical exponent characterizing the transition, even when the data is noisy or incomplete. We demonstrate the method's efficacy by applying it to experimental data from a silica-water suspension and a cornstarch-water suspension, successfully extracting the critical parameters for both.

This study introduces a novel methodology for modeling hourly electricity consumption during power crises, utilizing a Markov chain framework. The approach involves partitioning the day into discrete time intervals and assigning a state to each based on the number of available power sources. By employing a transition matrix to represent the probability of shifting between these states, the model generates a synthetic dataset of hourly usage. This synthetic data is subsequently compared against actual consumption records to evaluate the model's accuracy.

Personalization in search engines, such as Google, is intended to enhance user experience by delivering tailored results. However, this approach may inadvertently cause users to overlook pertinent information, potentially leading to suboptimal decisions. This study investigates the extent to which personalization can obscure relevant data. We conducted a controlled experiment involving 1,200 participants who were asked to locate specific information about a fictional company. The findings indicate that personalization can cause users to miss up to 20% of relevant results. Furthermore, the study reveals that users are largely unaware of this phenomenon, as they fail to recognize the personalization of their search results.

Program synthesis is a key area of computer science, yet existing methods often struggle with complex tasks like converting flow charts into code. This paper introduces GRCNN, a novel approach that utilizes a Graph Recognition Convolutional Neural Network to generate programs from flow charts. GRCNN employs a Graph Recognition Convolutional Neural Network to identify the specific operations within a flow chart and a Graph-to-Sequence Convolutional Neural Network to translate these identified operations into executable code. Experimental results indicate that GRCNN outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 10.5% improvement in accuracy.

This paper examines the application of reduction methods to climate dynamics, with a specific focus on the Lorenz model and the Lorenz-96 system. We explore how these techniques can be utilized to derive simplified models that retain the essential characteristics of the original systems.

The Os isoelectronic sequence, which includes Au IV, is examined using the FAC atomic code to generate transition probabilities and energy levels. These results are compared with existing literature, and the derived data are utilized to calculate the opacity of Au IV. The findings are then applied to model the kilonova ejecta resulting from neutron star mergers.

This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to automatically segment gastrointestinal (GI) regions within endoscopic images. The proposed method employs a two-stage architecture: first, a U-Net model segments the GI tract, and second, a ResNet model refines the segmentation by removing residual artifacts. The system was evaluated on the Kvasir dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.

Compositional data, defined as vectors of non-negative elements that sum to a constant, are prevalent in numerous scientific disciplines. This study introduces a linear algebra framework for analyzing such data, demonstrating that the standard simplex serves as a natural subspace within a larger vector space. We further examine the linear algebraic properties of the log-ratio transformation, a technique used to map compositions to the real number line. Additionally, we explore the geometric characteristics of the centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation and its associated covariance matrix. Finally, we outline a method for visualizing the covariance matrix of compositions in two dimensions.

We have analyzed the CORALIE/HARPS radial velocity dataset to investigate the occurrence rates of sub-Saturn mass planets (0.04–0.1 M$_{\rm Jup}$) orbiting solar-like stars. Our findings indicate that the frequency of these planets is comparable to that of super-Earths and mini-Neptunes, with a median occurrence rate of 0.04 per star. This result contradicts the hypothesis that sub-Saturns are rare, a notion previously suggested by the limited detections in the Kepler sample. Furthermore, we observe that the occurrence rate of sub-Saturns declines with increasing stellar mass, a trend that aligns with the findings of the Kepler mission.

This study introduces a novel method for regulating attention in deep neural networks by maximizing the mutual information between attended regions and the target class. We demonstrate that this approach yields superior performance compared to existing techniques, including those based on reinforcement learning, and notably, it requires no external reward signals.

We investigate the formation of dark matter clumps in the early universe, specifically examining scenarios where the interaction between dark matter and a mediator particle is Yukau-type. Our findings indicate that clump formation is significantly more probable in this context compared to the standard case of self-interacting dark matter. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the resulting clumps are more compact, possessing higher central densities and smaller radii. These characteristics suggest that Yukau-mediated interactions could explain the observed discrepancies between dark matter simulations and astronomical data.

We introduce a novel recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture that utilizes a fixed, sparse connectivity pattern. This design enables rapid learning across various cognitive tasks, including the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, the N-Back task, and the Tower of Hanoi. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance compared to existing RNNs, which typically require extensive training to master these tasks. Furthermore, the architecture's efficiency stems from its ability to maintain a compact set of internal states, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with training.

We establish a geometric framework for the moduli spaces of nilpotent algebras defined over a field of characteristic zero. This approach utilizes the concept of a "quasi-variety of nilpotent algebras," which serves as a generalization of the classical notion of an algebraic variety.

We investigate the impact of Compton scattering between relativistic AGN jets and the cosmic microwave background (CMB) on the AGN's evolution. Our findings indicate that this interaction can significantly alter the AGN's lifetime, potentially extending it by a factor of 100 or more. Consequently, the CMB's influence on AGN evolution is substantial, particularly at high redshifts.

We introduce a non-cinetic Lagrangian for gravity that is constructed from the Ricci scalar and the Ricci tensor's square, with the latter term weighted by a non-cinetic coupling constant. This framework allows for the derivation of the field equations, which are subsequently applied to a spherically symmetric, static spacetime to investigate the Schwarzschild solution.

This study introduces a novel method for registering medical image volumes, leveraging 3D SIFT for feature extraction and discrete SP-symmetry for feature matching. The proposed approach is evaluated against the state-of-the-art VoxelMorph framework, demonstrating superior performance in both accuracy and computational efficiency.

We present a multi-band photometric study of the eclipsing double-degenerate binary system SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, which exhibits a 40.5-minute orbital period. Our analysis of the light curve reveals that the secondary star is significantly fainter than the primary, with a magnitude difference of $\Delta V = 0.41 \pm 0.01$ mag. Furthermore, the primary star's radius is constrained to $R_1 = 0.10 \pm 0.01$ R$_\odot$, while the secondary's radius is $R_2 = 0.05 \pm 0.01$ R$_\odot$. These findings indicate that the system consists of two white dwarfs, with the primary having a mass of $0.52 \pm 0.01$ M$_\odot$ and the secondary $0.18 \pm 0.01$ M$_\odot$.

Global pooling layers are essential components in deep learning architectures, yet their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigates global average pooling (GAP) and global max pooling (GMP) by modeling them as optimal transport problems. We demonstrate that both operations correspond to specific variants of the Wasserstein barycenter problem. Furthermore, we introduce a novel pooling method, termed Wasserstein pooling, which is grounded in the Wasserstein barycenter framework. Empirical results indicate that this new approach outperforms both traditional GAP and GMP across various benchmarks.

We investigate the host galaxy properties of active galactic nuclei (AGN) across different classifications, utilizing the SDSS DR14 dataset. Our analysis reveals that AGN host galaxies are predominantly elliptical or lenticular, with spiral galaxies making up a smaller fraction. Furthermore, we observe that the host galaxies of radio-quiet AGN are generally more massive and possess higher stellar velocity dispersions than those hosting radio-loud AGN. Additionally, the orientation of radio-loud AGN is found to be more aligned with their host galaxy's major axis compared to radio-quiet counterparts.

This paper investigates flat rotational surfaces within four-dimensional Euclidean space, $E^4$, that exhibit a pointwise 1-type Gaussian map. We demonstrate that such a surface must be a minimal surface. Furthermore, we provide a complete classification of these flat rotational surfaces in $E^4$ possessing a pointwise 1-type Gaussian map.

Pre-training is a critical component of semantic segmentation, yet the optimal approach remains debated. This study evaluates the efficacy of pre-training using monocular depth estimation versus image categorization. Our findings indicate that depth-based pre-training yields superior results compared to categorization-based methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate that pre-training on depth estimation is more effective than on image categorization.

We introduce TCube, a neural framework designed to generate natural language descriptions for multivariate time-series data. Unlike previous approaches that rely on domain-specific knowledge, TCube operates independently of such constraints. It employs a dual-stream architecture: a time-series encoder that utilizes a multi-head attention mechanism to extract features, and a language decoder that constructs narratives by integrating these features with a vocabulary of domain-agnostic templates. We evaluated TCube on the UCR archive, a collection of 84 standard time-series datasets, and demonstrated that it outperforms existing methods in both automated and human assessments.

The ATLAS collaboration reports on measurements of CP violation and rare decays in beauty mesons, utilizing the LHC's proton-proton collision data from 2015 to 2018. This dataset spans an integrated luminosity of 140 fb⁻¹ at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The study presents updated results for the CP-violating phase in the $B^0_s \to J/\psi \phi$ decay, alongside new findings for the branching fractions of $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$, as well as the CP-violating phase in $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$. Additionally, the paper details the first observation of the $B^0_s \to \pi^+\pi^-$ decay and provides initial measurements of the $B^0_s \to K^+K^-$ branching fraction.

This study examines the Ising model defined on a Cayley tree, specifically focusing on the existence of weakly periodic Gibbs states that exhibit a period of two. We demonstrate that such states exist for all values of the interaction parameter and external field, provided the tree's order is sufficiently high. Furthermore, we establish that these weakly periodic Gibbs states are uniquely determined.

This study examines a specific category of hyperbolic Cauchy problems featuring coefficients that are sublogarithmic in time. We establish the global well-posedness of these problems, demonstrating that solutions remain bounded within a specific range of Gevrey classes.

Japanese term segmentation involves dividing Japanese text into meaningful units, a task complicated by the language's lack of explicit word boundaries. This study introduces a novel approach utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to address this challenge. The proposed method employs a two-stage pipeline: first, a character-level LSTM identifies the boundaries of terms, and second, a dictionary-based module refines these results by correcting any remaining errors. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that this system achieves a precision of 90.1%, recall of 90.0%, and an F1 score of 90.0% on the standard benchmark dataset.

Stack Overflow serves as a prominent platform for programmers to exchange knowledge, with external links being a primary method for sharing resources. This study investigates the characteristics of these external connections, specifically examining the types of sites shared, the nature of the content, and the user behaviors surrounding them. The analysis reveals that the majority of these links originate from Wikipedia, GitHub, and Stack Overflow itself. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that users who share external connections tend to be more active and possess higher reputation scores than those who do not.

The Galaxy Zoo project has gathered extensive data on galaxy morphology, revealing a rich variety of forms that challenge current theoretical models. This paper critically examines proposed solutions to the Galaxy Zoo diversity issue, evaluating their strengths and weaknesses. We argue that the most promising approach involves a combination of the "two-phase" model and the "two-component" model.

Climate change is a critical global issue that demands effective communication to drive meaningful action. However, the sheer volume of information and the complexity of the subject often hinder public understanding and engagement. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that leverages knowledge bases to facilitate climate dialogue. We present the Climate Knowledge Base (CKB), a specialized resource containing over 100,000 entities and 1.2 million relationships, which we constructed by integrating existing climate data with information from Wikipedia. We further developed the Climate Dialogue System (CDS), a conversational agent designed to support discussions on climate topics by utilizing CKB. We evaluated the CDS through a user study, demonstrating that it significantly enhances the quality of climate dialogue.

Symptom event extraction is a critical task in clinical natural language processing, yet existing methods often struggle to generalize effectively to unseen domains. This study introduces a new framework designed to enhance domain generalization in symptom event extraction by leveraging the inherent characteristics of clinical notes. Specifically, we propose a novel approach that utilizes a domain-specific neglect mechanism to filter out irrelevant information, thereby improving the model's ability to handle out-of-distribution data.

This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning framework designed for autonomous driving, where the agent's objective is to maximize cumulative rewards by selecting optimal actions. The system utilizes a convolutional neural network to process visual inputs and generate a probability distribution over possible maneuvers. To address the challenge of sparse rewards, we employ a reward shaping strategy that provides intermediate feedback to guide the agent toward the goal. Additionally, we propose a novel approach for generating training data from a single image, eliminating the need for extensive annotated datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques.

This study introduces a novel Spiking Random Neural Network (SRNN) designed for precise and energy-efficient classification. The architecture leverages the inherent randomness of its neurons and synapses, eliminating the need for complex weight training. Instead, the model utilizes a straightforward, unsupervised learning algorithm to adapt its parameters to the specific characteristics of the input data. The paper details the SRNN's architecture, its learning mechanism, and its performance across various classification tasks. The findings demonstrate that the SRNN achieves classification accuracy comparable to established methods while significantly reducing energy consumption.

This study investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark stars situated within an external magnetic field at finite temperature. The analysis employs the MIT bag model to derive the equation of state, which is subsequently utilized to determine the stellar mass-radius relationship. The findings indicate that increasing the temperature results in a reduction of the star's radius and a corresponding increase in its mass. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that a stronger magnetic field leads to a larger stellar mass and a smaller radius.

We introduce Pando, a personal assistant designed to operate within web browsers. Pando leverages a user's existing browser history to learn their habits and proactively suggest relevant content. It achieves this by employing a novel, lightweight, and privacy-focused machine learning model that runs directly in the browser. This model is trained on a dataset of 100,000 real-world browsing sessions, enabling it to predict user intent with high accuracy. We introduce a novel algorithm for approximating the eigenvalues of nonlinear eigenvalue problems (NEPs) of the form $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, where $A(\lambda)$ is a matrix-valued function. The method relies on minimal rational interpolation (MRI) to construct an approximate rational matrix function $\tilde{A}(\mu)$ from evaluations of $A(\mu)$ at selected nodes. The resulting eigenvalues of $\tilde{A}(\mu)$ serve as estimates for the original NEP's eigenvalues. We establish that the algorithm's convergence is adaptive, meaning it automatically adjusts to the problem's characteristics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the computational cost is comparable to that of existing methods.

We demonstrate that the intermediate $\beta$-shifts defined by $T_{\beta, \gamma}$ are conjugate to the class of "gapped" greedy $\beta$-shifts, denoted as $X_{\beta, \mathcal{G}}$. This result establishes a correspondence between the conjugacy class of $T_{\beta, \gamma}$ and the set of allowable gaps $\mathcal{G}$, which is determined by the parameter $\gamma$.

We present a comprehensive analysis of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking in $SO(N_c)$ gauge theories, utilizing the framework of the dual superconductor model. This approach relies on the hypothesis that confinement arises from the dual Meissner effect, where the vacuum behaves as a dual superconductor characterized by the condensation of magnetic monopoles. Within this model, the confining potential is described by a dual Abelian Higgs mechanism, and the resulting string tension is determined by the condensation scale of these monopoles. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the same mechanism responsible for confinement also accounts for chiral symmetry breaking.

We introduce a novel method for explaining Random Forests and similar tree-based models by utilizing Disentangled Attribution Curves (DACs). This approach relies on the concept of "disentanglement," which posits that distinct features within an input should independently influence a model's output. By employing a greedy algorithm, our method identifies the most impactful features and visualizes their specific contributions through DACs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing that it successfully isolates the influence of individual features and accurately reflects the model's internal logic.

Federated learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm that enables the training of models on decentralized data without exposing the underlying datasets. This approach is particularly valuable for privacy-sensitive applications, such as healthcare, where data cannot be shared due to confidentiality concerns. However, FL faces significant hurdles, including communication inefficiency, the need for a central server, and the vulnerability of the aggregation process to malicious actors. To address these limitations, this paper introduces FLACE, a new framework that leverages Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to facilitate secure, efficient, and decentralized model training. FLACE operates by distributing the learning process across multiple TEEs, ensuring that data remains private and the aggregation phase is protected from tampering. By eliminating the reliance on a central coordinator, FLACE offers a robust solution for privacy-preserving machine learning in hostile environments.

This paper introduces a novel method for automatically assessing drivers in embedded systems, specifically targeting those with minimal code footprints. The approach utilizes a custom-built, open-source, and freely available framework that generates a comprehensive set of test cases to verify driver functionality. The system's efficacy is demonstrated through the automated testing of a Linux kernel driver for the STMicroelectronics LPS21HB pressure sensor.

Containerized microservices are increasingly vital for modern applications, yet their dynamic nature introduces significant challenges in managing system calls. This paper introduces Timeloops, a novel framework that employs deep reinforcement learning to autonomously learn system call policies for these microservices. Timeloops operates by constructing a simulation environment that models the execution of microservices and utilizes a deep reinforcement learning agent to derive optimal system call strategies. The framework's efficacy is demonstrated through two distinct use cases: first, by generating system call policies that enhance the performance of existing microservices, and second, by creating policies that enable the execution of new microservices.

We introduce a novel framework for linear classification within the space of merchandise, utilizing a specific form of linear classifier. This approach is grounded in the concept of merchandise space forms, which are defined as linear spaces equipped with a positive semi-definite, symmetric bilinear form. We demonstrate that the resulting classifiers are highly effective, particularly for tasks involving the categorization of products.

This study examines the dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole (SMBH) within a galaxy, specifically focusing on the strong separation regime where the gravitational pull of the galaxy is negligible compared to that of the SMBH. We derive a new analytical formula for the stellar distribution function applicable to this regime, which is then validated against numerical simulations. Our findings indicate that the distribution function is highly sensitive to the initial conditions of the stellar population. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the distribution function remains stable over time, even when the system is perturbed by a passing star.

This study examines a linear system subject to random disturbances, where the objective is to minimize a quadratic cost function. The system's state and control inputs are constrained, and the proposed solution utilizes a stochastic model predictive control (MPC) approach. The paper demonstrates that this stochastic MPC method yields a superior outcome compared to a deterministic MPC strategy.

This study introduces a new framework for Compressive Singular Component Analysis (Compressive SCA), which aims to recover the singular vectors of a low-rank matrix from a limited set of linear measurements. We establish that the proposed method is capable of recovering these singular vectors with high accuracy, provided the measurement matrix satisfies the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP). Furthermore, we present an efficient algorithm designed to solve the corresponding optimization problem.

This study examines a noisy version of the voter model featuring a competition-colonization tradeoff, where species 1 dominates established territories while species 2 excels at colonizing new areas. We establish that species 1 excludes species 2 when the latter's colonization rate is insufficient, whereas coexistence occurs if species 2's colonization rate exceeds a specific threshold. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system's long-term behavior is governed by a quasi-stationary distribution.

We establish the category of local von Neumann algebras within the ground state of the abelian quantum double model. This category is shown to be equivalent to the category of local von Neumann algebras in the toric code model.

This study investigates a cavity magnomechanical system designed to generate tripartite entanglement among magnons, photons, and phonons. We demonstrate that incorporating a coherent feedback loop significantly enhances the fidelity of this entanglement. Furthermore, we analyze the system's robustness against various noise sources, revealing that the coherent feedback loop effectively mitigates the detrimental impacts of noise.

We present a comprehensive compilation of one-loop triple-collinear splitting operators for all possible parton combinations, derived using dimensional regularization. These operators are formulated in terms of the fundamental splitting functions and the corresponding one-loop anomalous dimensions of the relevant operators.
This paper presents a generalization of Grothendieck's Neron desingularization theorem, specifically for one-dimensional local rings.

This paper introduces the Suryakala-Nusantara project, which aims to document sundials across Indonesia. The initiative seeks to preserve sundials as significant cultural artifacts and to enhance public understanding of traditional timekeeping methods. The authors present a methodology for recording sundials, which includes a specific algorithm for calculating the time displayed by the Sundu Kaca, a sundial type utilizing a glass lens.

This study investigates a D2D communication system where cognitive radio principles are applied to Integrated Data and Energy Networking (IDEN) environments. Specifically, the D2D receiver utilizes a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) to enhance its ability to detect and decode signals from the IDEN source. The RIS is optimized to maximize the D2D receiver's harvested energy, thereby improving the overall system performance. The paper derives the closed-form cumulative distribution function (CDF) for the D2D receiver's harvested energy and subsequently obtains the closed-form CDF for the D2D outage probability. This study introduces a novel method for conducting two-dimensional measurements using a single-point Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV) system. The approach relies on a distant, single-point LDV setup to capture the vibration response of a structure, which is then processed to generate full-field 2D data. The methodology is validated through experiments on a cantilever beam, demonstrating that the resulting measurements align well with theoretical predictions.
We demonstrate that the satisfiability problem for first-order logic with binary relations is undecidable when restricted to first-order patterns.

Programmable phase plates (PPPs) have recently been introduced to enhance the resolution of transmission electron microscopes (TEMs) by compensating for spherical aberration. This study examines the performance of a PPP in a spherical aberration-corrected TEM, specifically investigating its ability to correct aberrations and its impact on image contrast and resolution. We demonstrate that a PPP can effectively correct spherical aberration, provided that the phase shift it applies is precisely matched to the specific spherical aberration coefficient of the objective lens. Furthermore, we show that a PPP can correct spherical aberration across a range of defocus values, enabling the use of a single phase shift to achieve optimal resolution over a broad defocus span.

This paper investigates the enumeration of random walk positions within the $L_1$-norm ball in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We establish that the count of such positions is asymptotically equivalent to the total number of possible walk locations, a result that extends a finding by Kozma and Wittenberg from the case of $d=2$ to arbitrary dimensions.

We investigate the extension of the Gambini-Olmedo-Pullin (GOP) quantum polymer singularity, which is constructed by joining two distinct Gowdy Taub-NUT spacetimes across their singular boundaries. This extension is achieved by applying the extended geometry framework originally proposed by Ashtekar and Gielen. We demonstrate that this extended structure exhibits a regular, non-singular core, which we analyze in detail. Furthermore, we calculate the quasinormal spectrum for scalar field perturbations within this extended geometry. Our findings indicate that the resulting quasinormal frequencies align with those of the original GOP model.

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of graphene sheets doped with electrons, specifically examining how finite-temperature screening influences the heat capacity. Our findings indicate that the heat capacity of these systems is governed by the temperature-dependent screening length, which is itself a function of both temperature and doping concentration.

This study introduces MaskedSpeech, a novel framework for speech generation that employs a masking strategy to enhance the contextual awareness of speech synthesizers. The system consists of two primary components: a masking module that generates a context-sensitive mask by integrating information from both preceding and succeeding segments, and a speech generation module that utilizes this mask to produce audio. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through experiments on the LJSpeech and LibriTTS datasets, where it demonstrates superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a new approach to predictive estimation that projects predictions into a latent space, where the target variable is assumed to follow a specific distribution. This method offers a unified framework for both probabilistic and non-probabilistic models, enabling the derivation of optimal estimators for both categories. We demonstrate that this technique can enhance the performance of existing models and provide a means to assess their reliability.

This study investigates adversarial attacks on machine learning classifiers by introducing a novel Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) framework. In this scenario, an adversary intercepts and alters the input data stream between the source and the classifier. We demonstrate that this approach enables the adversary to manipulate the classifier's output to any desired target class. Furthermore, we introduce a new class of generative models designed to facilitate these attacks and present a method for training them. Our experiments indicate that these models can be effectively utilized to execute MitM assaults.

This study examines the prevalence of climate change denialism on Twitter, specifically analyzing the frequency of hoax-related terms within the top 100 trending topics. The research utilizes a dataset of 100,000 tweets from 2019, employing a machine learning model to classify these posts as either hoax or non-hoax. The findings indicate that hoax-related content appears in 10% of the top 100 trending topics, with the most frequent instances occurring in the first half of the year.

This study presents a search for dark matter produced in conjunction with a single top quark or a top quark pair at the LHC, utilizing proton-proton collision data from the ATLAS experiment at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The dataset, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$, was collected during 2015 and 2016. The analysis examines final states containing one or two jets, one or two b-tagged jets, and one or more leptons (electrons or muons). The results are compared against Standard Model predictions and a range of dark matter models. No significant deviations from the Standard Model are observed. Consequently, the study establishes exclusion limits on the cross-section for single top quark or top quark pair production in association with dark matter, contingent upon the specific model parameters.

This paper investigates the n-extranged category of n-extraprojective modules over an n-extranged algebra within the framework of n-extranged categories. We establish Auslander-Reiten-Serre duality for n-extranged categories and demonstrate that the n-extranged category of n-extraprojective modules over an n-extranged algebra is equivalent to the n-extranged category of n-extrainslant modules over the same algebra.

This paper introduces a new instrumental variable framework designed for analyzing interventions that lack a specific ordering. It demonstrates that, under specific conditions, the average treatment effect on the treated can be identified using a single instrument. The authors apply this methodology to estimate the impact of college majors on lifetime earnings, utilizing the variation in major popularity across different states as the instrument. The findings indicate that the returns to majoring in STEM fields are significantly higher than those for non-STEM fields.

The BESIII experiment has recently achieved a milestone by collecting a dataset of 10 billion $J/\psi$ mesons, a feat that enables the production of a vast array of exotic hadrons. This paper outlines the capabilities of the BESIII facility for generating antineutrons and hyperons, which are essential for upcoming high-precision nuclear and particle physics endeavors.

We investigate the accretion dynamics within hierarchical triple systems featuring discs, utilizing a numerical framework that integrates the N-body simulation code REBOUND with the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code GIPHY. Our study examines the influence of disc mass and the orbital configuration of the system on accretion rates. We find that the presence of a tertiary body significantly enhances accretion speeds, with the magnitude of this increase contingent upon the specific orbital arrangement. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system's orbital configuration dictates the long-term evolution of the inner binary, with the most stable outcomes occurring in systems where the inner and outer orbits are coplanar and share the same direction of rotation.

We investigate the cosmological model of a lattice universe, which is inherently flat and devoid of a cosmological constant. This model is defined by a discrete set of matter fields, each possessing a specific mass, and is analyzed using the Euclidean path integral approach. We demonstrate that the model's dynamics are governed by a single parameter, $\alpha$, which is determined by the ratio of the lightest matter field's mass to the Hubble scale. We further show that the model's behavior is characterized by two distinct regimes: a high-$\alpha$ regime, where the universe is dominated by the lightest matter field, and a low-$\alpha$ regime, where the universe is dominated by the Hubble scale. We also discuss the implications of the model for the early universe and its potential to explain the observed acceleration of the universe's expansion.

This study introduces a novel variational segmentation framework that integrates image recovery techniques to enhance segmentation outcomes. The proposed model employs a hybrid approach, combining a Mumford-Shah functional with a total variation term to delineate object boundaries. Furthermore, it incorporates a specific image recovery method to boost segmentation performance. The resulting optimization problem is addressed using an alternating minimization strategy, which is proven to converge. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the model effectively segments images containing multiple objects and successfully handles noisy data.

We investigate the spin distribution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) within the heavy quasar population, utilizing the accretion disk's superradiance mechanism to constrain the properties of ultralight bosons. Our findings indicate that the spin distribution of heavy quasars is significantly narrower than that of the general SMBH population. This observation suggests that heavy quasars are likely to be young, having formed recently through mergers that impart high spins to the resulting SMBHs. Consequently, the spin distribution of these young, high-spin objects serves as a sensitive probe for detecting ultralight bosons.

Neuromorphic hardware is a rapidly advancing field that has recently seen significant progress in both simulation and physical implementation. This paper introduces Brian2Loihi, an emulator for Intel's Loihi neuromorphic chip, which is built upon the open-source Clyde simulator. By leveraging Brian2, a high-level Python-based spiking neural network framework, Brian2Loihi enables the rapid prototyping of complex models for Loihi. The tool is available as an open-source package on GitHub.

This study examines the evolution of a solar noise storm source during a microflare, utilizing high-resolution spectroscopic data from the IRIS and SDO/AIA instruments. The analysis reveals that the source's spectral line profiles exhibit a consistent, linked evolution across all parameters, including line width, asymmetry, and peak intensity. This coordinated behavior suggests that the observed changes are driven by a single, unified mechanism. The study attributes these dynamics to the interaction between a magnetic reconnection event and the subsequent relaxation of the stressed magnetic field. The findings offer valuable insights into the fundamental processes governing solar flares and noise storms.

We introduce a planar integrated magnetic optical trap (PMOT) designed to capture and retain ultracold atoms. This device combines a magnetic field generated by a microfabricated coil with a laser beam focused by a micro-optic lens. The PMOT's compact footprint allows it to be easily integrated with other micro-fabricated components, facilitating the creation of versatile, multi-functional atomic systems.

We investigate the accretion of a collisionless gas onto a black hole, where the gas is initially confined within a finite spherical region. The initial state is defined by a spherically symmetric distribution of energy and angular momentum, with the latter being uniform across all particles. The system's evolution is modeled using the Vlasov-Poisson-Einstein equations, and the results are compared against the standard Bondi model. Our findings indicate that the Bondi model fails to accurately represent accretion when the gas is restricted to a finite radius. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the presence of non-zero angular momentum significantly alters the accretion dynamics.

We investigate the interaction between an atom and a thin mirror, focusing on how the mirror's properties influence the atom's motion-induced stimulation and radiation. Our findings indicate that the mirror's thickness significantly impacts the atom's acceleration and the resulting radiation spectrum. Specifically, we demonstrate that a mirror with a finite thickness can enhance the atom's acceleration by a factor of up to 100 compared to a perfectly reflecting one. Additionally, we show that the mirror's thickness alters the spectral distribution of the emitted radiation.

This study presents new observations of Wd2, utilizing the VLT/ISAAC instrument to capture near-infrared data and the VLT/FORS2 instrument to capture optical data. The resulting catalog includes 1,000 sources, with 100 of these identified as massive stars. The paper analyzes the cluster's stellar population, specifically examining the distribution of massive stars and their evolutionary status. This study examines a normalized ground state for a specific type of biharmonic Choquard equation. The authors establish the existence of a normalized ground state solution by utilizing a minimization approach on a particular constraint set.

Handwritten document image enhancement (HDIE) is a critical task in the field of handwritten text recognition (HTR). Although current methods have achieved significant progress, they often struggle with the inherent variability in handwriting styles and the degradation caused by poor image quality. To address these limitations, we introduce a multi-task adversarial network designed to enhance HDIE performance. This approach employs a dual adversarial framework: a primary generator that refines handwriting style and legibility, and a secondary discriminator that evaluates the authenticity of the generated output. Additionally, we propose a novel multi-task loss function that simultaneously optimizes both image quality and recognition accuracy. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a system designed to extract data from Indonesian identity cards, which are currently difficult to read due to their complex layout and the presence of numerous tables. The proposed solution employs Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to convert card images into text, followed by Natural Language Processing (NLP) to parse and organize that text into a structured format. The system was evaluated using 100 identity card images, achieving an accuracy of 98.5% in text extraction and 97.5% in the final structured output.

This study introduces a novel time-averaging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework designed to enhance channel estimation for IEEE 802.11p. By leveraging the temporal averaging capability of the proposed LSTM, the system effectively mitigates noise and interference, thereby improving overall channel estimation performance. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach surpasses existing methods in terms of accuracy.

This study introduces a novel approach to astronomical image colorization and enhancement using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The proposed method involves two distinct stages: first, a GAN is trained to generate colorized images from grayscale inputs, followed by a second GAN trained to refine these results by removing artifacts and enhancing image quality. The effectiveness of this two-stage framework is validated through experiments on the Messier 101 galaxy image.

This paper introduces a novel gradient-free neural network architecture, termed the Universal Approximation Theorem-based Neural Network (UATNN). The proposed model relies on a specific universal approximation theorem that enables the representation of any continuous function on a compact domain using a network with a single hidden layer. The UATNN is designed to be both gradient-free and capable of handling both regression and classification tasks. The study demonstrates that this architecture can be trained effectively using the gradient-free Kaczmarz algorithm. Furthermore, the paper provides a theoretical analysis of the UATNN's generalization capabilities.

The ECFA Early Career Researcher's Committee (ECRC) was established in 2019 to champion the interests of young scientists within the organization. This document outlines the committee's composition, organizational framework, and activities during the 2021–2022 period.

We introduce a dual metasurface designed to manipulate line ripples, a phenomenon where a single beam splits into two parallel beams. This system utilizes two distinct metasurfaces, each engineered to impart a specific phase profile. By adjusting the separation between these layers, we can control the distance between the resulting parallel beams. This capability enables the creation of optical devices such as beam splitters and beam expanders.

This paper introduces a scalable, open-source cognitive AI architecture designed for large-scale multi-agent systems in Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC). The system is built upon a modular framework that integrates a cognitive model, a learning mechanism, and a planning engine, all of which are implemented using ROS 2 and Python. The architecture's modularity allows for the seamless integration of various cognitive models, learning algorithms, and planning strategies. To demonstrate its scalability, the system was applied to a multi-agent task learning scenario involving a team of robots and a human. The results indicate that the architecture can effectively support the deployment of complex cognitive AI models across extensive multi-agent environments.

This study introduces a bias-corrected estimator for the mean absolute deviation (MAD) around the median, a metric used to gauge the dispersion of a random variable. We establish the asymptotic normality of this estimator and demonstrate that it achieves asymptotic efficiency. Furthermore, we present a bias-corrected variant of the jackknife estimator for the MAD around the median, which is shown to be asymptotically equivalent to our proposed estimator.

Relation extraction (RE) aims to identify relationships between entities within a text, a task that is crucial for knowledge base construction and completion. This study introduces a novel approach to RE that integrates knowledge graph (KG) link prediction. Specifically, we utilize the predicted links from a KG to enhance the representation of entities in text, thereby improving the overall performance of relation extraction. Experimental results on the TAC RE dataset demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study investigates the properties of quarkonium dissociation within a thermal QCD medium, specifically examining the behavior of the quasi-particle Debye mass under finite baryonic chemical potential and momentum anisotropy across an N-dimensional space. We analyze the temperature and chemical potential dependencies of the Debye mass for both longitudinal and transverse modes, as well as the resulting impact on the dissociation of quarkonium states. Our findings indicate that the quasi-particle Debye mass increases with rising temperature and baryonic chemical potential, while momentum anisotropy causes it to decrease. Furthermore, we observe that the dissociation of quarkonium states is significantly influenced by the magnitude of the quasi-particle Debye mass.

We report the magnetic structure of Tb$_3$RuO$_7$, a compound featuring alternating spin-3/2 RuO$_2$ chains, as determined by neutron diffraction. The structure consists of two distinct phases: a low-temperature phase below 1.5 K and a high-temperature phase between 1.5 K and 15 K. In the low-temperature phase, the Tb$^{3+}$ moments form a commensurate antiferromagnetic structure, while the Ru$^{4+}$ moments exhibit a non-collinear antiferromagnetic arrangement. The high-temperature phase is characterized by Tb$^{3+}$ moments in a commensurate antiferromagnetic state and Ru$^{4+}$ moments in a non-collinear antiferromagnetic state. The magnetic structure of the high-temperature phase is attributed to the non-uniform internal magnetic field acting on the Ru$^{4+}$ moments, which arises from the Tb$^{3+}$ moments. Recent developments in functional illustration have produced visually compelling and aesthetically pleasing representations of periodic functions. However, these methods often lack generalizability, as they rely on specific functions and fixed parameters, thereby limiting their utility for broader applications. This paper introduces a novel approach to generating local functional illustrations that are both generalizable and adaptable. By employing a modulation technique, we demonstrate that periodic functions can be effectively represented through a combination of a base periodic function and a set of localized functional illustrations.

We introduce a new class of semi-generative models designed to address covariate shift, a scenario where the training data distribution differs from the target distribution. This approach integrates generative and discriminative techniques by learning a conditional distribution of features given the label to adjust for covariate shift, while simultaneously training a classifier on the resulting reweighted data. We demonstrate that this method is effective for both independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) settings and those involving dependent data, such as time series. Furthermore, we establish theoretical bounds on the excess risk of these models and provide empirical evidence through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Deep learning has achieved remarkable success across numerous fields, yet its internal mechanisms remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a geometric framework for analyzing deep learning, demonstrating that the training process can be modeled as a gradient descent trajectory on a specific loss function. By examining the properties of this function, we can derive insights into the behavior of deep learning systems.
We examine the impact of various terms on the effective potential within the $SU(2)$ gauge-Higgs model, specifically analyzing how these contributions affect the location of the potential's minimum.

This study introduces a novel method for enhancing the interpretability of machine learning (ML) jet taggers, which are essential for identifying physics processes within high-energy particle collisions. We demonstrate that incorporating variables with established physical significance into the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) improves their ability to explain their own decisions. Furthermore, we apply layerwise relevance propagation (LRP) to analyze the decision-making mechanisms of these DNNs. Our findings indicate that the trained models prioritize expert variables, thereby validating the physical logic embedded within the network.

This paper introduces a novel class of degenerate r-related Stirling numbers of the second kind, denoted as $\left\langle\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right\rangle_q^\xi$, and establishes their fundamental properties. We derive several recurrence relations for these numbers and demonstrate their connection to degenerate r-associated Lah numbers. Furthermore, we establish a relationship linking these degenerate r-related Stirling numbers of the second kind to degenerate r-associated Stirling numbers of the first kind.

This study examines the irreducible representations of single and double strata groups, categorized as either ordinary or gray types, with their symmetry properties derived from the site symmetries of the strata groups. The analysis covers both one-dimensional and two-dimensional cases, with the latter focusing on square, rectangular, and hexagonal lattices.

We examine the momentum operators associated with Killing vector fields whose integral curves are geodesics, demonstrating that these operators are essentially identical to those derived from Killing vector fields with constant norm. Furthermore, we establish that the corresponding momentum operators are Hermitian if and only if the underlying Killing vector fields are either null or possess constant magnitude.

The Hubbard sign problem, a major obstacle in Monte Carlo simulations of fermionic systems, is addressed by a new complex-valued neural network approach. This method utilizes a complex-valued autoregressive distribution to model the fermionic sign problem, with parameters optimized via a variational framework. The study demonstrates that this technique effectively mitigates the sign problem in the one-dimensional Hubbard model, achieving a significant reduction in statistical error.

We investigate composite Higgs models featuring a single composite sector, where the Higgs doublet and the associated pseudo-Goldstone bosons arise from the same source. In these frameworks, the Higgs mass is determined by the scale of compositeness, while the mass of the pseudo-Goldstone bosons is generated through explicit symmetry breaking. We demonstrate that the Higgs potential can be derived from the effective Lagrangian of the pseudo-Goldstone bosons, which is constructed using the same symmetry-breaking mechanisms. We further examine the implications of this approach for the Higgs self-coupling and the spectrum of heavy resonances.

Perceptual distortions in virtual reality (VR) are frequently viewed as detrimental to user experience, yet this study demonstrates that they can also serve as a powerful tool for enhancing it. We introduce a novel framework for analyzing VR distortions, which categorizes them into two types: those that degrade the experience and those that improve it. We argue that the latter category can be leveraged to create more engaging and immersive environments.

We introduce a methodology for integrating new languages into BigScience's multilingual framework, which is designed to enhance the quality of multilingual models. This approach involves training a language adapter for the target language using a small set of unlabeled data, which is then applied to the existing multilingual model. We demonstrate that this technique effectively improves performance on languages not previously seen by the model.

We investigate the formation of binary systems through the fragmentation of rotating cores, specifically examining how the initial mass of the system influences the resulting binary's total mass. Our findings indicate that the creation mass of the binary system is independent of the parent core's initial mass. Instead, the binary's creation mass is determined by the initial angular momentum of the core and the specific mass distribution within it.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm, M-ar-K-Fast, designed for autonomous analysis of magnetic resonance images (MRI). The method integrates the advantages of both K-Fast and Auto-K-Fast, specifically utilizing the automatic feature selection capabilities of Auto-K-Fast alongside the rapid convergence of K-Fast. The algorithm's performance is evaluated against the original K-Fast and Auto-K-Fast methods using both synthetic and real-world MRI datasets. The results demonstrate that M-ar-K-Fast achieves a faster convergence rate than Auto-K-Fast while maintaining comparable feature selection performance to both K-Fast and Auto-K-Fast.

This paper establishes a correspondence between the Choiceless Polynomial Time (CPT) and the extended polynomial calculus (PC), demonstrating that a graph property is definable in CPT if and only if it is provable in extended PC. We further show that CPT can decide the isomorphism of graphs with treewidth $k$ in time polynomial relative to $k$ and the input size, whereas the standard polynomial calculus cannot distinguish non-isomorphic graphs with treewidth $k$ in polynomial time.

This paper introduces a novel infinite family of $\sigma$-elementary rings, denoted as $R_{\sigma, n}$, which are constructed as subrings of the rational function field $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ and are generated by the set $\{1, t, t^2, \dots, t^n\}$.

This study examines the nature of unfalsifiable claims, which are statements that cannot be proven false. We demonstrate that such claims are not merely isolated anomalies but are instead organized within a coherent conceptual framework. This framework is defined by a specific set of attributes, and we show that these attributes are not arbitrary but are systematically linked. We also explore the origins of this framework, suggesting that it arises from the inherent properties of language itself. Finally, we discuss the implications of this framework for the study of human cognition.

This study introduces a novel approach to identifying traffic incidents in real-time by leveraging geotagged social media data. The methodology involves a two-stage process: first, a clustering algorithm groups posts based on their textual content, and second, a spatial-temporal algorithm detects incidents by analyzing the resulting clusters. The system's efficacy is validated using a dataset of 1.2 million tweets from the United States, demonstrating that it achieves a 90% recall rate with a false positive rate of only 1.5%.

We introduce a swift technique for analyzing the CMB lensing bispectrum, which is essential for investigating CMB lensing–large-scale structure (LSS) cross-correlations. This method relies on a skewing approximation that accurately models the bispectrum of the lensed CMB temperature and polarization anisotropies. We demonstrate that this approach achieves a high degree of accuracy, with errors remaining below 1% across all multipoles. Furthermore, we show that the method is computationally efficient, requiring only a fraction of the processing time needed by standard approaches.

We introduce a Bayesian framework for inferring the probability distribution of adversarial examples, utilizing a generative adversarial network (GAN) to model the data. This approach enables the calculation of the likelihood of specific adversarial instances, thereby allowing for the verification of robustness against those particular examples. We demonstrate the utility of this method by applying it to the classification of images and the detection of adversarial audio.

This study investigates the effects of dimensionality reduction on pixel classification within hyperspectral imagery, utilizing spectral dimensionality reduction (SDR) techniques. The research evaluates three SDR methods—Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Locally Linear Embedding (LLE)—by applying them to the Indian Pines dataset. The findings indicate that while PCA and LDA yield comparable classification accuracy, LLE outperforms both in terms of accuracy.

We introduce a compression framework for authentic language models, which are trained on real-world data. This approach is grounded in the hypothesis that genuine language models are inherently compressible. We demonstrate that this property can be leveraged to enhance the models' performance on authentic text. Furthermore, we present a novel compression method that surpasses the performance of existing techniques.
